definition: A felon is a person who has committed a felony. Status as a felon may affect the severity of punishments a person receives if they are convicted of future crimes. For example, in states with three strikes laws, a felon who is convicted of a third felony is subject to life in prison with no possibility for parole. Additionally, status as a felon may subject a person to laws they otherwise would not have been required to comply with. For example, per 720 ILCS 5/24-1.1, it is illegal for a felon to possess a firearm in Illinois. Due to the risk of recidivism, many states provide felon protection laws designed to reduce the chance a felon commits further felonies.
